newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may end commodity funds' minimum trade unit.
newsitem.headline: Japan may end commodity funds' minimum trade unit.

text.p: The Japanese government is considering abolishing rules that require a minimum investment in trading of commodity funds within the 1998/1999 fiscal year as part of an easing of regulations on the funds, a Trade Ministry official said on Friday.

The official said the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) has proposed that the minimum trading unit for commodity funds be lowered to five million yen in October 1997 and be abolished altogether by the end of March 1999.
The government has already decided to reduce the minimum trading unit for commodity funds to 10 million yen from April 1 from the current 50 million yen.
"The minimum trading unit of 10 million yen is still too much for individual investors, and has hindered a significant flow of money into the funds," the official said.
The plan is waiting for approval from the cabinet later this month.
A commodity fund is a financial instrument which puts investors' money into a wide range of markets, including soybeans, gold and oil futures.
